messages:
alex: Heads-up: after the v2.14 rollout we’re seeing continuous-batcher token/sec drop and big queueing delays on prod. P50 latency fine but P99 up ~4x. Blocking the rollout for now.

maria: Ack. Any bisect yet? Which hosts/regions affected?

alex: Started triage, affects us-east and eu-west, mostly high-concurrency routes. Quick numbers from the canary: token/sec from ~22k -> ~11k on same load. Queueing delay distribution shifted right.

tim: I pushed kernel-selection heuristic change in PR #2345 that landed in the release. It bumped kernel fallback priority for quantized kernels. Could be a bad path for short-sequence workloads.

perf-ci-bot: perf/regression: CI perf check failed on runtime-bench: p99_latency +320% on continuous-batcher test (job: ci/runtime/perf/bench-1123). Link: https://ci.redwood/test/1123

sre-bot: Alert: high_request_latency on redwood-batcher-prod-east-1, threshold crossed at 2026-03-18T09:12:42Z. Instances autoscaled.

maria: Can you paste the microprofile? flamegraph? Also check KV cache hit rate — if prefix caching got disabled we'll see more decoder work and smaller batches.

alex: Pasting abbreviated perf capture (sampler + timelines):
```
timeline: queue_delay_ms p50=8 p90=42 p99=210
kernel_exec_ms p50=1.2 p90=3.5 p99=12.8
tokens_per_sec: before=22000 after=11050
kv_cache_hit_rate: before=0.71 after=0.69
batch_size_mean: before=18.3 after=9.6
```
Seems mean batch size halved.

tim: That lines up with kernel heuristics picking a different execution path that increases per-token exec time and reduces effective batching (more frequent smaller batches due to changed scheduling thresholds). I can repro locally with the new kernel selector toggled.

opsana: Rollout hold is on. Any quick mitigation other than revert? Could we pin routes to older model variant or force kernel hinting?

maria: We tried forcing kernel hint via env `KERNEL_HINT=legacy_fast` on one canary and token/sec recovered to ~20k, batch sizes back to ~17. So kernel choice is causal.

tim: Ok bisect result: regression introduced by PR #2345 (commit 3f2a1b9). The change was intended to prefer quantized kernels for memory savings but didn’t account for scheduling interop with continuous-batcher thresholds.

alex: Proposal: revert 3f2a1b9 from release branch to un-block rollout, then open follow-up to: 1) add an integration perf test for continuous-batcher + kernel-selection combos, 2) refine heuristics to consider batch-size distribution, 3) KV cache integration check. Thoughts?

maria: +1 to revert ASAP. Add a canary that forces legacy kernel for 30m after revert then resume. Also add an automated guard in CI that fails releases if token/sec drops >20% on benchmark.

tim: I’ll prepare the revert PR and include unit test to ensure we don’t flip kernel for workloads with mean batch > 8. Also adding a flag to kernel-selector to expose a scoring penalty when continuous-batcher is enabled.

opsana: Revert PR ready: https://git.redwood/pr/2890 revert(3f2a1b9). Applying to release branch now. Scheduling maintenance window for canary verification.

perf-ci-bot: CI run queued for revert PR: job ci/runtime/perf/bench-2890.

alex: After revert applied to canary, quick check shows tokens_per_sec back to baseline (~21.6k), batch_size_mean ~17. Avoiding full rollout until green CI and 30m canary.

maria: Please follow up with a postmortem doc that includes: root cause analysis (kernel heuristics + scheduler interaction), perf traces, test gaps, and the planned long-term fix. Assign owners for each item.

tim: Will own kernel selector fix. Alex will own CI guard and perf test. Maria will handle postmortem writeup. Opsana will coordinate rollout.

alex: Thanks all — keeping rollout paused until CI + canary pass. Adding labels: rollback, perf-regression, blocking-release. :white_check_mark:
